topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Probability

outline.topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Probability

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Conditional Probability
sections.content: Briefly recap the definition of conditional probability: P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B). Use a visual Venn diagram to show the 'reduction of sample space' when event B is known to have occurred.
sections.example: A bowl contains 10 fruits: 6 apples (4 red, 2 green) and 4 oranges. Visual highlight: If we know the fruit is an apple, the sample space shrinks from 10 to 6.

sections.title: The Concept of Independence
sections.content: Define statistical independence: Events A and B are independent if P(A|B) = P(A). Explain that knowing B gives no information about A. Represent this visually as two separate, non-overlapping circles in a probability space.
sections.example: Flipping a coin (Event A: Heads) and rolling a die (Event B: Rolling a 6). The outcome of the coin flip does not shift the probability of the die roll.

sections.title: Introducing Bayes' Theorem
sections.content: Introduce Bayes' Theorem as a method for 'reversing' conditional probability. Formula: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B). Use a tree diagram to show how we start from a cause (A) and work backward to evaluate the likelihood of that cause given an effect (B).
sections.example: A 'Robot Doctor' diagnoses a patient. If the patient has a symptom (B), how do we update the probability of a specific disease (A) based on the test accuracy?

sections.title: Synthesis: Applying Bayes in Real Scenarios
sections.content: Connect the concepts: Show how Bayes' Theorem behaves when events are independent versus dependent. Emphasize that Bayes is the engine behind machine learning classifiers like Naive Bayes.
sections.example: A cat detector algorithm: If the cat is 'Fluffy' (A) and it is 'Daytime' (B), assume independence to simplify the calculation: P(A|B) = P(A). But if B is 'Meowing', independence fails, and we must use the full Bayes' formula to update our belief about which cat is in the room.

sections.title: Summary & Conclusion
sections.content: Recap: Independence simplifies probability (multiplication rule), while Bayes' Theorem provides a systematic way to update our beliefs as new evidence arrives. Final visual: A scale balancing prior belief against new evidence.
sections.example: Final thought: 'Probability is not a fixed number, but a dynamic update.' Use a quick 10-second animation of a 'Belief Bar' moving toward 100% as more evidence is gathered.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: Conditional Probability
lecture_lines: Conditional probability shrinks the sample space.
Formula: P(A|B) equals P(A intersection B) over P(B).
Visualizing the reduction clarifies the relationship.
animations: Fade in label for Conditional Probability. Highlight P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B).
Animate intersection of two sets A and B.
Show denominator P(B) as the restricted sample space.
Flash the formula components to show correspondence.
Transition to the next section with a smooth wipe.

storyboard.title: The Concept of Independence
lecture_lines: Independence means one event does not influence another.
Knowing B provides zero info about A.
animations: Display two circles A and B completely separated.
Fade in P(A|B) = P(A) to show no effect.
Highlight the lack of intersection region.

storyboard.title: Introducing Bayes' Theorem
lecture_lines: Formula relates P(A|B) to P(B|A) and P(A).
Use it to update beliefs with new evidence.
Start from cause, move to effect.
animations: Highlight P(B|A) as the likelihood component.
Show P(A) as the prior probability component.
Animate the denominator P(B) expanding to full sum.
Final equation zoom and pulse for emphasis.

storyboard.title: Synthesis: Applying Bayes in Real Scenarios
lecture_lines: Bayes applies differently based on event independence.
Independent events simplify the calculation significantly.
Naive Bayes leverages this independence assumption.
Dependent events require the full formula.
Real world scenarios often mix these structures.
animations: Display medical test diagram for Bayes application.
Fade in probabilities for True Positive/False Positive.
Animate calculation flow to the final result.

storyboard.title: Summary & Conclusion
lecture_lines: Bayes' Theorem enables systematic belief updates.
Probability dynamically updates as evidence arrives.
animations: Fade in key takeaways from all previous sections.
Reiterate Bayes' Theorem as a central summary point.
Animate fade out for all visual components.
